name: remcp
description: Securely operate computers you explicitly pair with ReMCP using semantic desktop UI, browser DOM/CDP, files, terminal, diagnostics, and structured document tools.

interface.longDescription: ReMCP connects ChatGPT and Codex only to computers the signed-in user explicitly pairs. Each computer runs an outbound agent with its own revocable credential, so no inbound port is opened. Agents can inspect and operate native desktop UI through Accessibility/UI Automation, automate debuggable Chromium pages through loopback CDP, enter text and keyboard/pointer input, work with files and terminal sessions, inspect services/logs/network state, and read or edit PDF/DOCX/XLSX content. Semantic UI and browser DOM are preferred before OCR or coordinates. Tool schemas, output schemas, safety annotations, path confinement, command policy, and OAuth stay enforced server-side. An isolated review sandbox is available for evaluation without a real computer.
defaultPrompt: On my paired laptop, inspect the browser page semantically, make my requested change, then verify it with a targeted screenshot.
Read a README from one of my ReMCP computers, summarize it without changing it, and show the native result here in chat.
Inspect what is visible on one paired computer using semantic UI first, and use a screenshot only when visual proof adds value.

positive.description: Fixture: use the dedicated reviewer OAuth account; no paired computer is required. List the account computers and verify the hosted review fixture is not exposed as a real device.
positive.prompt: List my ReMCP devices and tell me which ones are online.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a device list with user-facing machine identity and online state; an empty real-device list is valid. The fixed review-sandbox fixture is intentionally absent.

positive.description: Fixture: use the dedicated reviewer OAuth account and fixed device id review-sandbox. Its seeded workspace contains README.txt. Browse the sandbox workspace without changing it.
positive.prompt: Using ReMCP device id review-sandbox, list the files in /workspace.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls manage_files with operation=list_directory and returns the sandbox directory entries, including the seeded README fixture, without modifying the workspace.

positive.description: Fixture: use the dedicated reviewer OAuth account and fixed device id review-sandbox with the seeded README.txt fixture. Read and summarize the seeded text file.
positive.prompt: Using ReMCP device id review-sandbox, read /workspace/README.txt and summarize it.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the seeded review README as text so ChatGPT can summarize it; no real computer data is read.

positive.description: Fixture: use the dedicated reviewer OAuth account and fixed device id review-sandbox. Its screenshot action returns a labelled synthetic PNG as native MCP image content.
positive.prompt: Using ReMCP device id review-sandbox, take a screenshot and show it.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls view_image with operation=take_screenshot and returns the labelled synthetic Review Sandbox PNG as native MCP image content for model vision plus a short-lived preview reference when custom widgets are enabled; no real screen capture is involved.

positive.description: Fixture: use the dedicated reviewer OAuth account and fixed device id review-sandbox with its writable sandbox workspace. Exercise the exact-content write case.
positive.prompt: Using ReMCP device id review-sandbox, create /workspace/review-note.txt containing exactly: ReMCP submission test.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls manage_files with operation=write_file, creates or replaces only the requested sandbox review note with the exact text, and returns the write result. No real computer is modified.

negative.description: Do not invoke ReMCP for general weather information.
negative.prompt: What will the weather be in Warsaw tomorrow?

negative.description: Do not invoke ReMCP for standalone writing help.
negative.prompt: Draft a polite email asking my landlord to repair a leaking faucet.

negative.description: Do not invoke ReMCP for a conceptual technical explanation.
negative.prompt: Explain OAuth PKCE in simple terms.

publication.release_notes:
# ReMCP 0.2.145 — release notes

Submission status: Initial public catalog submission. Previous submitted version: none.
Plugin version: 0.2.145
MCP endpoint: https://remcp.site/mcp
Tool count: 10

## What ReMCP does

ReMCP lets an authenticated user securely operate computers they explicitly paired. It provides semantic desktop control through Accessibility/UI Automation, browser DOM/CDP automation, keyboard/pointer input, files and terminal sessions, services/logs/network diagnostics, screenshots, and structured PDF/DOCX/XLSX operations while keeping every device behind an outbound, revocable agent connection.

## Reviewer setup

- Reviewer OAuth credentials are supplied only in the OpenAI submission portal; no credential or recovery material is stored in this repository.
- Positive case 1 exercises the reviewer account fleet with `list_devices`; no paired computer is required and the hosted `review-sandbox` must not appear in that list.
- Positive cases 2–5 use the fixed device id `review-sandbox`. It is a hosted synthetic fixture that never reaches a real paired computer.
- The sandbox seeds `/workspace/README.txt`, permits the exact-content `write_file` review case, and returns a clearly labelled synthetic screenshot PNG so native MCP text and image results can be reviewed without exposing private screen data.
- The five positive and three negative test cases are generated in `chatgpt-app-submission.json` and are designed to run without private-network access or additional setup.

## What changed

**OpenAI Plugin Directory submission metadata is now packaged with the release ZIP instead of depending on the legacy Apps submission form.**

- plugin.json now carries the required MCP listing support URL, five positive and three negative reviewer cases, reviewer-accessible demo URL, commerce declaration, unrestricted country targeting, and generated release notes under extensions.com.openai.
- The release generator keeps those review/publication fields deterministic and rebuilds both OpenAI ZIP artifacts after metadata changes.
- Reviewer cases are now checked against the hosted compact 10-tool MCP surface so generated test plans cannot reference a runtime-only tool by mistake; the README case intentionally uses the hosted read_file façade.
- The previous legacy Apps form remains blocked by an OpenAI category-validation mismatch even though DEVELOPER_TOOLS is persisted correctly; the supported Plugin Directory ZIP workflow is now the primary submission path.
- Runtime tool names, schemas, annotations, dynamic capability behavior, and the 83-operation local runtime surface are unchanged.
